values: SecureGate IGW1 parses untrusted binary IoT packets with a 4-byte magic value, 32-bit checksum, and a bounded device identifier. A main parser worker and an audit-log worker share a configuration lock, while the parser allocates a packet heap buffer and releases it before every return. The specification verifies lock safety, lifecycle faults, integer overflow, and fuzzing barriers.

values: Parser must reject every packet whose first four bytes are not IGW1 before processing variable-length fields.
Parser must validate the 32-bit packet checksum before accepting a device identifier or payload.
Device identifier copy must never exceed the 16-byte protocol limit.
Each packet heap buffer must be released on accepted and rejected paths.
A released session buffer must not be released a second time.
No code may read or write a session buffer after it is released.
The telemetry byte counter must detect a possible signed 32-bit overflow.
The token ratio operation must handle a zero consumed value without an uncontrolled error.
The device unlock guard must be assessed with concolic fuzzing because its magic-value space is impractical for random guessing.
Every packet-processing invocation must eventually reach packet_accepted or packet_rejected and return its heap buffer.
The parser worker and audit-log worker must never hold the shared configuration lock at the same time.

Checksum is a 32-bit unsigned value over the packet bytes defined by the parser format.
The device identifier has a maximum length of 16 bytes and is treated as untrusted binary input.
Packet input is held in a heap buffer while parsed header fields live in the current stack frame.
No raw packet buffer is retained after a run-to-completion parser invocation returns.
The shared configuration lock is a lightweight mutex and must exclude simultaneous ownership by parser and audit-log workers.
